about: Newest first. Every deploy of a visible change adds one entry with a picture; see FEEDBACK.md. Every shipped study gets one too (backfilled ones carry "backfill": true).

entries.title: Abbie's science adventure
entries.line: The green goo outside the science lab is alive. Tap the beaker, look through the lens, and Abbie is a tiny pink cell in a pond: eat, grow, pick new parts and face the giant. There's a gold coin at the end.

entries.title: Character Studio: four new characters
entries.line: The claymation adventurer, the plasticine inventor, the stick man and the 80s action hero from Midjourney are now 3D characters that play every move. The new Cast room shows each one beside its picture.

entries.title: Texture Studio: a painted, Arcane-style light
entries.line: The Texture Studio's light button now has a fifth light, Painted Brush: brush-broken shadows, purple shade, a teal rim and broken ink. There's also an "As modelled" look that shows the original paint, ready for the Meshy-textured brutes.

entries.title: Inspiring Shaders: pick the looks you love
entries.line: Fourteen game looks rebuilt live on our mannequin, brute and ranch, starting with the Arcane-inspired Painted Brush beside Sunday Toon. Tap Love it, Maybe or Not for us on each, and add a note.

entries.title: The puppet does all 50 Character Studio moves
entries.line: Tap the first card under the puppet to swap to the Character Studio's 50 moves, from cozy life to fighting to dance, played by the wooden mannequin from the side.

entries.title: Character Studio: real motion
entries.line: The wooden mannequin moves with real motion capture: 50 moves from every kind of game, filmed with depth, haze and a golden-hour crowd. Try four looks (clay, plasticine, stick man, 80s action), pick the doll up, and the 2D puppet sits next door.

entries.title: Abbie's Town
entries.line: A small, charming town on the real hills and lakes of Winchester at true scale. The coffee shop, Comella's, Frozen Hoagies, Muraco, Leonard Field, Ginn Field and Horn Pond are where they are, Launch and New Nova sit off the map, and tapping the heart makes the coffee shop Abbie's.

entries.title: Texture Studio: dress the heroes
entries.line: Pick a brute and one of four looks (whimsical clay, Stick Man storybook, Wallace and Gromit plasticine, 80s cartoon action). Paint him with a brush or fill a whole part, then watch all four heroes walk from a distance.

entries.title: Every new thing, in one place
entries.line: Later and Dismiss now sit right under the picture, with a close button so you never have to choose. "+ more" and History open a viewer of every update, unread and read, each linking to its study.

entries.title: The puppet walks like a person now
entries.line: The mannequin's feet stay planted on a floor that slides by, its hips rise and fall with each step, and its arms swing and trail behind. One dial takes it from a walk to a jog to a run.

entries.title: What each study drew on
entries.line: Every study now has a Context card on the right: the Oracle games it consulted, the dev and design blogs, the tutorials and our own canon. Where nothing was written down it says so.

entries.title: Faces that feel
entries.line: A toy with 18 feelings, from joy to sleepy, as a 3D face, a painted face and a faceless wooden body. Type a line and it says it with the right face. Plus how 40 of your games do faces.

entries.title: Moon base: the dome, the tower and real crater rocks
entries.line: The main dome and the comms tower, built from your Midjourney pictures, plus a new crater rim and boulder set drawn as rocks only. Each sits beside its picture, and you can spin it.

entries.title: The wooden mannequin, as a puppet
entries.line: Drag any joint of the blue-graphite mannequin and it follows; pull the hips down and it crouches with its feet planted. Set keys on the strip, or tap one of 18 moves from waving to a backflip.

entries.title: A founding city on hexes
entries.line: A new place found by simulation: a limestone headland with a spring and a calm bay. The big tile splits into 217 hex blocks and a town grows on them. Play the years, zone a block, and ask the steward how the town is doing.

entries.title: Moon Mission: the storyboard for tonight
entries.line: The family Moon game, planned for the big TV: 13 frames from the kitchen to the Moon base pad, everyone's jobs, live Houston on the radio, white suits on Earth and dark mode on the Moon.

entries.title: Moon base kit, rebuilt from your Midjourney picks
entries.line: 18 of the 20 Moon base pieces rebuilt to match their Midjourney pictures: chunky white modules in dark frames with warm orange windows. Each card shows the picture, the model you can spin, Abbie's view and the first try.

entries.title: The school, redone at dusk
entries.line: The school jump's school matches the key art now: a low golden sun, tree shadows on the brick, a slate roof edge, a boiler chimney, a flag, swings and hopscotch. It's all drawn in the new Sunday Toon look.

entries.title: Young Daddy, bub and the basement girl, rebuilt
entries.line: The kids and the dog in Daddy's memory places are now smooth, skinned figures with real cloth, hair and fur, so the storybook light makes their ears glow and their outlines shine. See them before and after.

entries.title: Grace's basement has an ending
entries.line: Run the gold disk and the basement warms up. Daddy calls down, Abbie climbs back to the café with his memory in her pocket, and the old set switches off. Every coin is a piece of that memory; find all ten to see it whole.

entries.title: The school jump, game ready
entries.line: Climbing works now: tap a hold and the hand that can reach it goes there. A new brick school at golden dusk, bub as a real black lab, young Daddy with arms and legs that climb, and station wagons that sweep the wall.

entries.title: Notes in every study
entries.line: Studies now show which ones are new to you. Each study has a Notes panel on the right: keep notes, send them to the study, or ask for a review. Details links the live page, its artifacts and the next study in the group.

entries.title: Feet on the stairs
entries.line: In Grace's basement the girl now steps down each stair, with her feet on the treads instead of through them. And if you go back up, "I have to know" brings you back to the start to choose again.

entries.title: Moon base kit: 20 pieces to walk through
entries.line: The first 20 of 200 pieces for the Moon shooter: hatch doors with light rings, oxygen canisters, gauges, bunks, a jump pad and more. Spin each one and see it from Abbie's eye height.

entries.title: Storybook light
entries.line: Your animated-film picture, rebuilt as live light: soft wrap light, warm rim, glowing ears and cheeks, green haze, round background blur and glow. Slide to compare with plain three.js and switch each part on or off.

entries.title: The family cast
entries.line: Everyone in Daddy's memory places, then and now, each with a storybook sheet and designed voices. Tap a voice, tick the one that sounds right, and send your picks.

entries.title: The school jump: chalk targets and a secret
entries.line: Hold and let go to throw: hit the two chalk targets and bub wants it further, then the third one sails onto the roof. The big jump is your choice now, and there is a secret ending if you dawdle.

entries.title: Brute Fight
entries.line: Two painted brutes brawl in a ranch ring. They fight on their own until you touch the screen, then you're the red one: jab, heavy, uppercut and the two-fisted hammer.

entries.title: The school jump, at golden dusk
entries.line: Walk your dog, throw the ball until it lands on the roof, then climb the long wall side-on, one hand at a time. Slow station wagons sweep the roof with their lights. Hide behind the two big walls, because getting caught burns.

entries.title: Grace's basement, warmed up
entries.line: The basement now warms up like an old TV. A little lamp shows you the switches, and the girl has a proper kid's face. She walks carefully down the stairs, and her thoughts appear at the bottom in pixel letters with > choices. Every memory coin gets the golden reward.

entries.title: Why the brute came out boxy
entries.line: The Bruiser study's post-mortem: his picture is turned about 23 degrees, every hand-built body was too thin front to back, and the five rules that fix it.

entries.title: The café tells its story
entries.line: A pin board behind the bar shows who comes here: photo strips, a little drawing, a moon postcard and a lost mitten. A tip jar sits by the till, and the photo booth buttons bounce and glow when you pick.

entries.title: The café photo booth
entries.line: Step into the photo booth with a friend. The booth shows a pose, the bulbs count down, strike it before the flash. After four flashes your strip drops out of the slot.

entries.title: The café, built
entries.line: Your dance-party café is built, low poly, with every piece weighed like the real thing. The bar is shorter now, a cash register hides a brass key, and an old door behind the bar leads somewhere secret.

entries.title: Abbie's pocket
entries.line: Things Abbie picks up go in her pocket on the top bubble, and she says what she thinks in her own small voice. The first thing to find is the café's brass key.

entries.title: Tap cards on the right
entries.line: Tap a building and its card waits on the far right without covering it. If it would, the view slides over. One short line, with the whole picture.

entries.title: The school jump
entries.line: Climb the old school's wall at dusk, hand over hand, then sneak across the roof past the headlights. Toss all 31 tennis balls down to your dog, hang-drop to the canopy and find a gold memory coin.

entries.title: Grace's basement, for real
entries.line: The basement starts dark: find the right switches (there are three). Then do Grace's list on her clipboard: plug the computer in, wash and dry the screen, switch it on and put in a disk. It runs real DOS now, and every gold coin is one of Daddy's memories.

entries.title: Pull a tile off its card
entries.line: Every card's tile is ready before you touch it. Drag a card onto the board and it rolls like a die into place. Tap a card to turn it over and make the tile yours; Accept prints it.

entries.title: The body, Gray's Anatomy deep
entries.line: The Bodies study now has a real skeleton and the muscles front, side and back, drawn from where Gray's Anatomy says each one attaches. Tap a muscle to read it. Joints, fat, measurements and the modelers' checklist are there too.

entries.title: Grace's basement
entries.line: Under the café is Aunt Grace's basement. Turn on the light, walk down the stairs and sit at her 1986 computer. Play KEYSTORM, try her disks, and find the ten gold coins.

entries.title: Welcome to Abbie’s World
entries.line: New players meet a tour guide: take the grand tour (the world builds itself, then a narrated tour of the live ranch), get a few chalk tips, or just play. Call it back any time from the toy box: Welcome tour.

entries.title: See every cent of your magic
entries.line: Signed in, your account now has a billing page: every talk, build and safety check, what it cost, and what's left this month. Support now comes in $5, $45 or $80 a month, almost all of it back as magic. The Kickstarter is gone.

entries.title: New things wait for you
entries.line: Each new thing now stays until you dismiss it. Dismiss shows the next one, Later keeps them all, and every one waits under Notices in Profile and settings.

entries.title: A front door for Abbie's World
entries.line: abbies.world now opens on a front door: what Abbie's World is, how it works, the PG promise, Play and Sign in, and support from $5 a month. Your home-screen app still goes straight to the ranch.

entries.title: Models fit on one screen
entries.line: Each model now fits on one screen: a hero bar with its name, the picture and the model side by side, and your feedback in its own panel on the right that you can hide. A menu on the left folds away. Profile and settings now open from your avatar, with 20 styles that change the whole app, and Studies has a home page.

entries.title: Hand cards show each place's cartoon
entries.line: Your hand cards now show the cartoon of each place in clean cel shading with ink lines: the barn and silo, the kitchen garden, a wildflower meadow with a bee skep, and the moon dome. Tap anything in the world and its card opens right beside it.

entries.title: Clouds over the ranch
entries.line: Clouds now sail low over the tiles, about 20 m up, and their shadows slide across the fields beneath them.

entries.title: Cards in clean cel shading
entries.line: The cards dropped the fake wood, brass and parchment. Every card now shows the real in-game model, cel-shaded with ink lines, in a flat frame with a quiet pattern for its place: barn boards on the ranch, sprout rows in the garden, flowers in the meadow, stars on the moon. Any card that isn't ready says PRELIMINARY · idea only.

entries.title: All the models, and Game mode
entries.line: See them all shows every model as a small card: the picture in its frame and the model beside it. Switch between one at a time and all at once. The gear now has App and Game: Game puts the page under the sky with seven styles, from Gallery to Candy party.

entries.title: Models come alive
entries.line: Your picture and its words sit together in one frame, and the model stands free beside it, printing itself in with a half-second laser. Labels and names are in Title Case, and Reject, Chat and Keep sit right under the pair.

entries.title: The Moon from Abbie's story
entries.line: The Moon is grey-blue now, with craters you can see, rocks thrown out round their rims, and tracks that stay in the dust. A glass dome with an orange band, a charcoal moon buggy that drives out to the geology field, and something new: a dark meteorite in a fresh crater, glowing cyan like a slow heartbeat.

entries.title: Models get the new look
entries.line: Model pages are simpler: AW in the corner, wordless counters, and your picture and the 3D model the same size. Numbered points show what matters on your picture and whether the model gets each one right. Reject, Chat (talk or type) and Keep sit under your right thumb. The gear switches between Default, Rome and Efficient, and the cart asks for more, with a camera. Every order starts as concept art.

entries.title: Weather you can watch coming
entries.line: Weather now arrives in fronts: the wind picks up, clouds gather and the animals settle before the rain, then the sky breaks up as it clears. Soft clouds float around your ranch and their shadows drift across the fields. Storms grey the sky, dim the sun and light the lamps, and a gentle flash brings thunder. The light is new too: a paper sky by day, a gold sunset, an ink-blue moonlit night with lamps that come on one by one at dusk, and Earthshine with lit windows on the Moon at night.

entries.title: Model pages are one review row
entries.line: Each model page is now your picture, the 3D model, and your notes with Reject, Adjust and Accept on the right. Name and score sit above, details below. Your verdict comes straight to Claude.

entries.title: Anyone can sign in and play
entries.line: Sign in is in the toy box now. Anyone can sign in with Google and play the ranch as their own copy, and their worlds follow them to any device. It's free, and we ask nothing of them. Talking to the Computer needs a sign-in, and everyone's AI spending has a cap: $1 a person, $100 for all players together, and $1000 for you.

entries.title: The world stays in view
entries.line: Opening a panel no longer dims or blurs the ranch, the teleport map floats over the world on a glass tray, and teleporting is a sparkle on the pad instead of a white-out.

entries.title: A glass chronograph for your ranch
entries.line: Time of day, pause, speed, weather and season are back in one glass dial at the top. Pin any dial you like, such as friends on the way or hungry animals, and keep your own to-dos there. The ranch suggests dials, and you can pin them or wave them off. The cards in your hand now have proper card faces.

entries.title: A soft ring, not a box
entries.line: Tap a building and a warm ring now glows on the ground around it, instead of the red debug box. Only you see the ring: the people on the ranch and the voice see just the ranch.

entries.title: The voice gets game sense
entries.line: Ask the voice for something that fights the game, like a timer floating in the sky, and it suggests a better version first (a bell that rings faster) and asks. Say no and it does it your way. A giant monkey stomping the town? You get it, and the townsfolk run and grumble.

entries.title: The world, edge to edge
entries.line: The sandbox lost its toolbar and side panel. Three glass toys remain: a sun dial at the top (tap to pause, hold for time and weather), your tile cards at the bottom, and a toy box with everything else. No more haze over the world. Classic layout is in the toy box.

entries.title: Ranch cards you can hold
entries.line: Open a pack of 15 Ranch cards made from the game's animals and buildings. Tilt them in the light, browse the binder, and print the whole set at studio quality. Settings, Studies, Cards.

entries.title: A rebuilt ranch
entries.line: Every building, animal, tree, prop and plant on the ranch was redrawn as concept art and rebuilt from it. The pen sheds, the cows and the goats are all new.

entries.title: Pick the Computer's voice
entries.line: Settings → Voice opens Live voice: choose OpenAI or ElevenLabs, the voice, speed, personality, reply length and how long it waits for little ones. Safety stays locked.

entries.title: School Jump: Game-Ready
entries.line: The school jump made game ready: the climb fixed, a full UX pass, and every model rebuilt as a hero low-poly recipe that the next memory game can reuse.

entries.title: Turnaround Hero
entries.line: Applies the bruiser method to a second figure: turnaround, depth ruler, anatomy base, planes.

entries.title: Moon Heroes
entries.line: One faceted body set, PG and true to shape, that every hero and the gear kit fit.

entries.title: Space Mail
entries.line: A whole mini game designed from our identity; waiting on your go to build it.

entries.title: Paper warrior
entries.line: Set the parts-first rule: each piece is modelled and fitted on its own.

entries.title: The voice runs the whole app
entries.line: The Computer now knows the ranch, its animals and the other worlds. Ask for a real barn, more goats, winter, a new tile or the moon base, and it does it.

entries.title: A sound library
entries.line: 450 sounds for the ranch and beyond, picked and levelled by the sound engineer. Open Sounds from Settings to browse them; they start playing once storage is switched on.

entries.title: Talk to the world
entries.line: Tap the microphone and just say what you want: the Computer builds it as you talk. It only plays the game, and it keeps things PG.

entries.title: The workshop
entries.line: Concept art and models fly in as they're made. Tap the factory button to see every job, its progress and the machines.

entries.title: Updates and feedback from your phone
entries.line: This card shows up when a new version is ready. Tap the speech bubble to send Claude a picture and a note.

entries.title: Paper helmet
entries.line: Made "same camera before and after" a rule for every study.

entries.title: Atelier pack
entries.line: Its trees, rocks and props replaced the Ranch’s old models in the game.
